The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.530/2014 vide its judgment and award dated 25.02.2017.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 12.12.2013 when he was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-25/X-5636, which was rear ended by a bus belonging to the Maharastra State Road Transport Corporation Limited (henceforth referred to as 'Corporation')
bearing registration No.MH-20/BL-2439 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle').

entities.text: Maharastra State Road Transport Corporation Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
As a result,
the claimant fell off the bike and suffered injuries on his head, fracture of four ribs and other injuries.
He was shifted to Vijay Clinic Omerga and thereafter shifted to Yashodhara Hospital Solapur, where he was treated as an inpatient between 12.12.2013 to 07.11.2014.

The claimant claimed that he was 32 years old and was doing sanitary work, earning a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month and that due to the injuries suffered, he could no longer be employed and was thus deprived of the ability to earn income.
He therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the driver of the offending vehicle and Corporation.
3. The claim petition was contested by the Corporation who denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimant for compensation.

It contended that since both the vehicles were involved in a head on collision, both of them were responsible for the accident and the owner and insurer of the motorcycle were also proper and necessary parties.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1.
He examined two doctors as PW.2 and PW.3, who assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 30% to 35% to the whole body.
The claimant marked documents as Exs.P1 to P26.
However, the Corporation did not lead any evidence.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

It also held that the claimant had suffered injury on the right forehead, fracture of frontal bone and fractures of four ribs on NC:
2023:KHC-K:5507 the left side.

The Tribunal considered the evidence of PW.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered permanent disability to the extent of 30% to 35% to the whole body as fractures of the ribs were not properly united.

The Tribunal therefore, assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 5% to the whole body and his notional income was considered at a sum Jakir vs Sharad Ashok Patil And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149103144/

The Tribunal directed the Corporation to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is in appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the claimant had suffered five fracture injuries and that the claimant being a sanitary worker, these fractures affected his avocation and therefore, the Tribunal while considering disability suffered must have not only considered the physical disability but also the functional ability which were impeded.

He submitted that in the fact and circumstances of this case and in the light of the evidence of PW.2 and PW.3, the Tribunal must have considered the disability to the extent of 25% to 30% to the whole body.
He also contended that the accident happened in the year 2013 and therefore, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.
He also contended that the compensation awarded under the other heads warrants enhancement.
Per contra, the learned counsel for the Corporation submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the Corporation.

sentences.text: The fact that the claimant had suffered injuries in the road traffic accident that happened on 12.12.2013 involving two vehicles is not much in dispute.
The claimant had suffered fracture of the frontal bone as well as the fracture of four ribs on the left side.
The evidence on records disclose that the fracture of ribs were not united.

Therefore, this would cause permanent discomfort and disability to the claimant and the Court could not have downplayed the contention of the claimant that the injuries had caused immense disability and discomfort.

Having regard to the nature of avocation of the claimant and the injuries suffered as well as the evidence of PW.2 and PW.3, this Court considers it appropriate to assess the disability suffered by the claimant at 15% to the whole body.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5507 claimant, the notional income of the claimant ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.
The compensation awarded under the other heads also being meager warrants marginal enhancement.
11. Consequently, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-

Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Pain and suffering 50,000/-
 2
Medical expenses 3,10,019/-

3 Loss of income during the period 14,000/-
 of treatment for two months

4 Loss of income due to disability 2,14,200/-
 5

Attendant charges, food and 27,000/-
 nourishment, conveyance  charges  6 Loss of amenities 30,000/-

Since the liability of the Corporation is undisputed, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
13. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.4,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.6,45,219/-, which is NC: 2023:KHC-K:5507 payable by the Corporation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
14.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the Corporation before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
15. Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
